title: The workout was never the whole story.
deck: Risk of dying, compared with the least active 25% of adults

annotations.detail: Half the risk, one step up

_provenance.paper: doi:10.1136_bmj.l4570 · Ekelund et al. 2019, BMJ · systematic review + harmonised meta-analysis of 8 accelerometry cohorts, n=36,383, median follow-up 5.8y, 2,149 deaths
_provenance.axis: The paper reports quarters of the study population ranked by accelerometer-measured TOTAL physical activity; medians per quarter are not in the abstract, so x = population percentile with points at quarter midpoints (12.5/37.5/62.5/87.5). The counter counts percentile, not minutes — nothing on screen implies measured activity volumes.
_provenance.reference: First quarter (least active) — HR 1.00 by definition; the (12.5, 100, 'baseline') point is the comparator, not a reported estimate

claims.quote: 0.48 (95% confidence interval 0.43 to 0.54) in the second quarter
0.27 (0.23 to 0.32) in the fourth quarter (most active)

_provenance.copy_grounding: 'Any intensity counts' ← abstract: 'Any physical activity, regardless of intensity, was associated with lower risk of mortality'. 'Half the risk, one step up' ← c4 (−52% in the second quarter vs the first).
_provenance.reveal_test: Headline names the workout belief and withholds the rest of the story; the curve supplies it (total movement, any intensity) and the −73% endpoint is the completion payoff. 'THE BIG DROP' flag is on screen from t≈0.2s while the baseline segment holds — the stake lands before the plunge. Founder direction 2026-08-21: additive spin ('there is more than the workout'), never anti-gym — the audience trains.
_provenance.honesty: Total-activity arm only. The MVPA arm (c1–c3: −36/−45/−48%) is weaker than the total arm and goes to the caption, explicitly attributed — it is the evidence FOR the headline, not a second curve.
